title: Setting out: пойти, поехать — and сходить, съездить

blocks.text: The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").

items: Где старшина?
Where is the M/Sgt?
Он пошёл в штаб.
He went to (left for) HQ.

blocks.text: Note. — that the vowel -ё- in the verb "пойти" occurs in the masculine form only: пошёл, пошла, пошло, пошли. The future perfective (пойду, пойдёшь) belongs to the 1st -ё- type of conjugation. The future perfective (поеду, поедешь) belongs to the 1st -е- type of conjugation.

The perfective verb полететь (like пойти and поехать) denotes single action with the emphasis on the completed start. The past perfective (полетел, -ла, -ло, -ли) is formed in a regular way. The future perfective (полечу, полетишь) belongs to the 2nd (-и-) type of conjugation. The consonant "т" changes into "ч" in the first person singular only.

items: Полковник полетел в Вашингтон.
The Colonel flew to Washington. (single action; completed start)
Завтра я полечу на фронт.
Tomorrow I'll fly to the front. (single action)

blocks.text: The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech, e.g.:

items: Он пошёл к другу.
He went to a friend's place (and has not returned; unidirectional perfective).
Он шёл к другу.
He was on his way to a friend's place (unidirectional imperfective).
Он ходил к другу.
He used to go to a friend's place (multidirectional).
Он сходил к другу.
He went to a friend's place (and has returned; see prefixed perfective forms of motion verbs below).

по- and с- with ходить, ездить, летать

Adding a prefix to the repeated function verbs: ходить, ездить/езжать/, летать usually does not form the perfective aspect but merely changes the meaning of the original verb: ходить — to go, уходить — to leave. However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs.

a) Prefix "по-" denoting a perfective action of limited duration (an action "for a while"). The prefix "по-" when added to the "repeated function" verbs — ходить, ездить, летать — forms perfective verbs: походить, поездить, полетать. These verbs denote a single completed action of limited duration, similar to the verb "погулять".

items: Он походил по комнате и сел за стол.
Мы поездили по городу и поехали домой.
Я хочу полетать на самолёте.

blocks.text: b) Prefix "с-" implying a single round trip. The prefix "с-" when added to the "repeated function" verbs — ходить, ездить, летать — forms perfective verbs: сходить, съездить, слетать. These verbs denote a single trip (going to and coming from a place), especially when a quick return is implied.

items: Мне надо сходить на почту за письмами.
Я съезжу на вокзал и узнаю, когда отходит поезд.
Он сходил в библиотеку и взял книгу.

blocks.text: Note the preposition: after "going verbs" or the verb "to send" the preposition "за" + Instr. is used to indicate the idea of "going after" or "sending for" something or somebody: Он пошёл за газетой. — He went after the newspaper. Пошлите за доктором. — Send for the doctor.

exercises.why: **побежали** is the past tense (plural) of **побежать** (to start running, to break into a run) — the perfective of **бежать**, «set out». past: он побежа́л · она побежа́ла · оно побежа́ло · они побежа́ли. — Wiktionary, «побежать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Note the preposition: after "going verbs" or the verb "to send" the preposition "за" + Instr. is used to indicate the idea of "going after" or "sending for" something or somebody: Он пошёл за газетой. — He went after the newspaper. Пошлите за доктором. — Send for the doctor.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  The other choices: **бегали** is a form of **бегать** (to run); **бежали** is a form of **бежать** ((imperfective only) to run, to be running).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Unprefixed verbs of motion, which are all imperfective, divide into pairs based on the direction of the movement (uni- or multidirectional — sometimes referred to as determinate/indeterminate or definite/indefinite). (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Не ___ (сбегать — to run there and back) с концерта!
exercises.why: **сбегайте** is the imperative (вы, plural or polite) of **сбегать** ((colloquial) to run (to a place) and get back, to run (for), to go and get) — the perfective of the many-directions verb, meaning one trip there and back. imperative: сбе́гай · сбе́гайте. — Wiktionary, «сбегать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «b) Prefix "с-" implying a single round trip. The prefix "с-" when added to the "repeated function" verbs — ходить, ездить, летать — forms perfective verbs: сходить, съездить, слетать. These verbs denote a single trip (going to and coming from a place), especially when a quick return is implied.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
